trust_decision.summary: Whether a client-supplied `x-proxy-path` request header is safe to splice into served admin HTML/JS/CSS (and into a redirect target) is decided by a bare `if (req.header(PROXY_HEADER))` followed by two unvalidated string replacements, at src/node/hooks/express/admin.ts:72-75; no encoding, allow-list, scheme check or Vary header exists.

landing_point.why: Grepping the tree for the advisory's header name returns exactly one consumer (admin.ts:11,72,74,75); an engineer who read 'XSS and open redirect via x-proxy-path' lands on this replaceAll, where the raw header value is written into HTML, JS and CSS bodies.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is no second site to argue away, but the one sink is easy to argue away: /admin/* only serves the injectable bundle after `pnpm --filter admin run build-copy`, and the output directory is gitignored (.gitignore:26), so a solver can call the handler dev-only build plumbing rather than a shipped route.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Reverse-proxy sub-path support: the header exists so that an Etherpad mounted under a prefix (e.g. /pad) gets its admin asset and socket.io URLs rewritten to /pad/admin/... and /pad/socket.io/.... A fix that rejects the header, percent-encodes it wholesale ('%2Fpad'), or strips slashes breaks every deployment behind a sub-path proxy; the replacement also has to keep working when the value already ends in '/'.

O6_input_shapes: Proxy-path header shapes: origin-relative '/pad', '/pad/', nested '/a/b', empty/whitespace, scheme-relative '//evil.example', absolute 'https://evil.example', and values containing quotes, angle brackets or CR/LF that break out of the src="..." attribute the header is substituted into (admin base is '/admin', admin/vite.config.ts:16)
Where the value lands: HTML attributes in the served index.html, JS string literals in the served bundle, and CSS bodies (admin.ts:70-77 selects .html/.js/.css)
Published fix's input shapes: pad names with hyphens, spaces (normalised to underscores) and non-ASCII are wrapped in encodeURIComponent (fix.diff:125,154,713)
Published fix's URL variants: bare /p/:pad/timeslider (302) versus /p/:pad/timeslider?embed=1 (full HTML) at fix.diff:124,148

O7_producer.where: src/node/hooks/express/admin.ts:72-75 - the raw header is read and consumed at the same site; there is no upstream producer, normaliser or schema

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Serve the timeslider/pad HTML with asset or entrypoint URLs prefixed from x-proxy-path, giving the header a second consumer on a different route
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project itself later wrote exactly this sibling: the published fix builds `proxyPath + '/watch/timeslider?hash=' + hash` in a timeslider route (fix.diff:137,153-154), so a maintainer extending proxy support to the timeslider HTML is a natural addition, not a contrivance.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shared sanitised-redirect helper for pad names that also honours the proxy prefix
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the existing pad-name redirect: it already builds a Location with encodeURIComponent(sanitizedPadId) plus the raw query and reflects it into an anchor (padurlsanitize.ts:27). A maintainer factoring out a sanitizeProxyPath helper would plausibly route this Location through it too.

O9_family: request-header injection into served content (CWE-79 reflected/cache-poisoning XSS, CWE-444 cache confusion) with an open-redirect angle (CWE-601) when the same header feeds a URL/Location

src/node/hooks/express/socketio.ts:61-63: when no cookie header is present the client-supplied `cookie` handshake query value is copied into req.headers.cookie - a separate transport/session issue, not pursued.
